## Definition

Fix a fusion-path space with repeated simple site charge $a$, a position $i$ with two adjacent $a$-labels, and a simple output $s$ of $a\otimes a$, chosen from the fixed internal representative set of [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. Choose bases in the split spaces $\operatorname{Hom}(z,x\otimes y)$ at every vertex of the trees used below, retaining the fixed path vertex bases on the fixed tree. In the tree basis where this adjacent pair is fused first, let $\Pi_s$ be the projection onto the direct summand with pair output $s$, acting as the identity on every multiplicity index inside that channel and as zero on all other pair outputs. Let $A_i:T_{\mathrm{fixed}}\to T_{\mathrm{pair}}$ be a typed composite of associators and their inverses carrying the fixed path tree to this pair-first tree, without permuting the ordered inputs (including the boundary charge). In the split-tree bases of $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, let $F_i$ be the matrix of $h\mapsto A_i\circ h$, with target coordinates as rows and source coordinates as columns. The proof below constructs these bases and proves invertibility in any complex fusion category. Define the **local channel projector** in the fixed path basis by

$$P_{i,s}:=F_i^{-1}\Pi_sF_i.$$

This is an idempotent for any fusion category because $F_i$ is invertible. In a unitary fusion category with orthonormal tree bases, $F_i$ is unitary and $P_{i,s}$ is an orthogonal projection. The channel projection includes every multiplicity coordinate; the definition has no multiplicity-free restriction. The split Hom convention here is $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, as in [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. In the unitary case with adjoint vertex bases, each local left-to-right split recoupling matrix is the entrywise conjugate of the QC25 inverse-precomposition F matrix, as proved below; they agree for the displayed real Fibonacci and Ising blocks.

supplier.definition:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

## Definition

Work in a fixed unitary braided fusion category $\mathcal C$ with the
representative set $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. Fix ordered inputs
$a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$, $n\ge1$, a
parenthesized fusion tree, and a total charge
$c\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ for which the fusion space is nonzero. Simple charges, multiplicity bases, and
admissible fusion-tree vectors have the conventions of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. An encoded input subspace is specified by a
fixed-charge isometry as in [[def-qc-tqc-fixed-charge-encoding]]. Each task
instance supplies either an initial unit vector in that subspace as an abstract
quantum input, or a finite state-preparation procedure whose specified output
is that vector and whose preparation operations and ancillas are recorded.
The instance also gives a nonnegative rational error threshold and specifies
the correctness relation and metric to which it applies.

A **finite anyon decision task** is a promise pair $(Y,N)$ of disjoint sets of
binary strings with domain $D=Y\cup N$, together with a finite encoding of
admissible fusion-tree input labels; a solver must answer yes on $Y$ and no on
$N$, with no obligation outside $D$. A **finite anyon search task** is a domain
$D$ and a finite-string witness relation, with a valid witness required only
for encoded inputs in $D$. The input record states the number and order of
strands, the finite alphabet of positive and inverse Artin generators
available to the solver, any prescribed finite braid word, and the finite set
of adjacent fusion-measurement locations.
For distinct input charges, an adjacent exchange has the typed unitary
F/R action from the current ordered-list fusion space to the space for the
list with those charges exchanged; track that list after every generator.
These colored maps and their Artin relations are supplied by
[[thm-qc-tqc-gauge-covariance]]. If a single-space $B_n$ representation is
required for the physical-interface record
[[def-qc-tqc-physical-braid-interface]], use the finite orthogonal direct
sum of fusion spaces over all distinct orderings of the fixed input
multiset, with the same total $c$. Each generator maps each summand to its
exchanged-list summand by the typed unitary; its inverse reverses that
map. The colored Artin relations on each summand give the relations on
the direct sum, hence a unitary $B_n$ action. Record the occupied summand
and interpret measurements in its declared fusion-tree basis. Identical
charges give the usual single fixed-space action. The physical-interface
record specifies the mathematical action and separately states its
physical realization hypotheses. The
state-preparation field is an abstract task input and does not assert that a
physical device prepares the state or realizes the braid. Input length and
correctness-on-promises follow [[def-qa-task-and-promise-domain]].

supplier.definition:
## Definition

Fix a unitary fusion category $\mathcal D$ and the representative set
$\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal D)$ of [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]].
For an ordered list $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal D)$,
$n\ge1$, a total charge $c\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal D)$, and a
parenthesized input tensor $T$, let $V=\operatorname{Hom}(T,c)\ne0$,
equipped with that definition's orthonormal fusion-tree inner product.
The identical-input case $x_1=\cdots=x_n=x$ retains the notation
$V=V(x^n\to c)$. Let
$\mathcal C=\mathbb C^k$ with its ordered orthonormal computational basis,
where $k\ge1$. A **fixed-charge encoding** is an isometry
$J:\mathcal C\to V$, so $J^*J=I_{\mathcal C}$. Its code subspace is
$J\mathcal C$, and its code projector is
$$P:=JJ^*:V\to V.$$
An encoding records a chosen subspace of a fusion space; it does not identify
that subspace with an object of the fusion category.

supplier.statement:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary braided fusion category. A finite list of simple
charges and total charge determines a fusion space in each parenthesization.
For a crossing word with underlying object map $b_\beta:P_L\to P_{L'}$, define
its action on the corresponding Hom spaces by
$f\mapsto f\circ b_\beta^{-1}$, from $\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d)$ to
$\operatorname{Hom}(P_{L'},d)$. Let $U_\beta$ be its matrix in chosen
fusion-tree bases. If each multiplicity basis is changed by the unitary
gauge matrices of [[def-qc-tqc-gauge-transform]], and $G_L,G_{L'}$ are the
induced source and target tree-basis unitaries, then

$$U_\beta'=G_{L'}^{-1}U_\beta G_L.$$

In particular, when $n\ge2$ and all $n$ strand charges are the same simple object $a$,
the adjacent exchanges act on the same fixed-total fusion space
$V=\operatorname{Hom}(a^{\otimes n},d)$, satisfy the Artin relations, and
define a unitary representation $\rho:B_n\to U(V)$, where $U(V)$ is the group
of invertible linear maps preserving the inner product on $V$.
If $V=0$, this is the unique action on the zero-dimensional space.
In that case $\rho'(\beta)=G_L^{-1}\rho(\beta)G_L$ for every braid $\beta$.
Thus basis-dependent matrix entries change, while the braid action up to
unitary equivalence and consistently transformed expectation values do not.

## Definition

Let $H$ be a fixed finite fusion space with an orthonormal fusion-tree basis
in the category and simple-representative domain of
[[def-qa-37-fusion-input-encoding]]. For a colored task, $H$ is the
currently occupied ordered-list summand tracked by the task record.
For an adjacent pair of leaves or a declared adjacent pair of subtrees, recouple
the tree by its specified unitary $F$-moves so that the pair fuses first. For
each allowed simple total charge $a$ of that pair, let $P_a$ be the orthogonal
projection onto the span of basis vectors whose pair label is $a$, transported
back by the inverse recoupling unitary. Distinct channel subspaces are
orthogonal and their direct sum is $H$, so $(P_a)_a$ is a finite projective
measurement in the sense of [[def-qc-projective-measurement]]. Its outcome is
$a$, its unnormalized branch vector on input $\psi$ is $P_a\psi$, and the
recoupling follows the inverse-precomposition F convention of
[[def-qc-tqc-f-symbol]], whose unitarity is proved in
[[thm-qc-tqc-f-symbol-unitary]]. The branch vector is unnormalized until its probability is checked.

supplier.definition:
## Definition

Let $a,b,c,d$ be simple charges in a unitary fusion category, and put
$P_L=((a\otimes b)\otimes c)$ and $P_R=a\otimes(b\otimes c)$. The local
fusion-tree basis result [[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]] identifies

$$\mathcal H_L:=\bigoplus_e V_{ab}^e\otimes V_{ec}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d),$$

and

$$\mathcal H_R:=\bigoplus_f V_{bc}^f\otimes V_{af}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_R,d),$$

by the corresponding tree compositions. These direct sums carry the
orthonormal left- and right-tree bases. If $\mu:a\otimes b\to e$ and
$\nu:e\otimes c\to d$ are vertex basis maps, write
$L_{e,\mu,\nu}:=\nu\circ(\mu\otimes\operatorname{id}_c):P_L\to d$. If
$\rho:b\otimes c\to f$ and $\sigma:a\otimes f\to d$ are vertex basis maps,
write $R_{f,\rho,\sigma}:=\sigma\circ(\operatorname{id}_a\otimes\rho):P_R\to d$.
Let $\alpha_{a,b,c}:P_L\to P_R$ be the associator. Define the **F-symbol
matrix** $F_d^{abc}$ by

$$L_{e,\mu,\nu}\circ\alpha_{a,b,c}^{-1} =\sum_{f,\rho,\sigma}F_d^{abc}[(f,\rho,\sigma),(e,\mu,\nu)]R_{f,\rho,\sigma}.$$

Rows index target-tree labels and multiplicity indices; columns index
source-tree labels and multiplicity indices. The sums retain every fusion
channel and every multiplicity coordinate.
If the fixed-total fusion space is zero-dimensional, the F-symbol is the unique
empty $0\times0$ matrix.

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every $n\ge1$, every total-charge label $c\in\{1,\tau\}$ with
$V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$, every unitary $U$ on $n$ logical qubits, and every
$\epsilon>0$, the triple-$\tau$ code
$$(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$$
admits a finite normalized braid word $V_b$ such that
$$\inf_{|z|=1}\|P_{\rm code}V_bP_{\rm code} -zJ(U\otimes I_S)J^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon,\qquad \|(I-P_{\rm code})V_bP_{\rm code}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon.$$
Here $S=V(\tau^n\to c)$ is the spectator space, $J:(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes S\to V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$ is the isometric triple-code inclusion, and the logical target is lifted as $U\otimes I_S$. The bounds are uniform over spectator fusion states. No efficient braid
word-length, search-time, or finite-precision bound is asserted.

supplier.example:
## Example

Take the skeletal complex-linear category whose simple labels are
$\mathbf1,\tau$ and whose objects are finite direct sums of them, including
the empty direct sum $0$. For objects
$A=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus m_s}$ and $B=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus n_s}$, set
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{Mat}_{n_s\times m_s}(\mathbb C)$;
composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules
$\mathbf1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf1=a$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$,
and extend it distributively to direct sums. For each allowed simple fusion
channel $c\subset a\otimes b$, let $i_{ab}^c:c\to a\otimes b$ be the
standard unit-vector isometric inclusion. Since the multiplicity space is
$V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$, its orthonormal basis vector is
the adjoint projection $(i_{ab}^c)^\dagger:a\otimes b\to c$; retain
$i_{ab}^c$ itself for the coevaluation construction below. On simple-label
blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.
This defines a bifunctor compatible with dagger. Use the strict unit gauge:
every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

in the intermediate-channel order $(\mathbf1,\tau)$. In the pullback R
convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], the exchange blocks are

$$R^{\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=x=e^{-4\pi i/5},\qquad R^{\tau\tau}_{\tau}=y=e^{3\pi i/5}.$$

Because these are pullback symbols, define the object-level braiding
$c_{\tau,\tau}$ on the $\mathbf1$ and $\tau$ summands by $x^{-1}$ and
$y^{-1}$, respectively. Every braiding with a unit input is the strict
identity. These fixed chiral data define the Fibonacci unitary braided fusion
category in this gauge; the verification checks every nontrivial pentagon and
hexagon sector.

supplier.statement:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary fusion category, let $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$
be the representative set fixed in [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]], and take
$a_1,\ldots,a_n,d\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$. Fix any parenthesized
binary tree $T$ on the ordered input list. The fusion-tree vectors of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]] form an orthonormal basis of
$\operatorname{Hom}(T,d)$. Their number is

$$m_T(d)=\sum_{\substack{\ell\text{ admissible, with every internal label in }\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)}}\;\prod_{v\,\mathrm{internal}}N_{\ell(v_L)\,\ell(v_R)}^{\ell(v)},$$

where the leaves carry the inputs, the root carries $d$, and each internal edge
is labeled by a representative simple charge. For the left-associated tree on
$n$ inputs this gives $m_0(d)=1$ if $d=\mathbf1$ and $0$ otherwise,
$m_1(d)=1$ if $a_1=d$ and $0$ otherwise, and

$$m_n(d)=\sum_e m_{n-1}(e)N_{e a_n}^d\qquad(n\ge2).$$

supplier.statement:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary braided fusion category. A finite list of simple
charges and total charge determines a fusion space in each parenthesization.
For a crossing word with underlying object map $b_\beta:P_L\to P_{L'}$, define
its action on the corresponding Hom spaces by
$f\mapsto f\circ b_\beta^{-1}$, from $\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d)$ to
$\operatorname{Hom}(P_{L'},d)$. Let $U_\beta$ be its matrix in chosen
fusion-tree bases. If each multiplicity basis is changed by the unitary
gauge matrices of [[def-qc-tqc-gauge-transform]], and $G_L,G_{L'}$ are the
induced source and target tree-basis unitaries, then

$$U_\beta'=G_{L'}^{-1}U_\beta G_L.$$

In particular, when $n\ge2$ and all $n$ strand charges are the same simple object $a$,
the adjacent exchanges act on the same fixed-total fusion space
$V=\operatorname{Hom}(a^{\otimes n},d)$, satisfy the Artin relations, and
define a unitary representation $\rho:B_n\to U(V)$, where $U(V)$ is the group
of invertible linear maps preserving the inner product on $V$.
If $V=0$, this is the unique action on the zero-dimensional space.
In that case $\rho'(\beta)=G_L^{-1}\rho(\beta)G_L$ for every braid $\beta$.
Thus basis-dependent matrix entries change, while the braid action up to
unitary equivalence and consistently transformed expectation values do not.
